title: Jonah IQ
subtitle: How well do you know the runaway prophet?

questions.text: To which city did God first tell Jonah to go and preach?

options.explanation: Tarshish was the place Jonah fled toward, in the opposite direction. It was not where God sent him.
Jonah 1:2 says, "Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry against it." Nineveh was the capital of Assyria.
Babylon plays a big role elsewhere in Scripture, but it is not where Jonah was sent.
Joppa was the port where Jonah boarded a ship to run away, not his assigned destination.

questions.text: Instead of obeying, where did Jonah try to flee?

options.explanation: Jonah 1:3 says he rose up to flee unto Tarshish, going down to Joppa and boarding a ship to run from the presence of the Lord.
Egypt is a common refuge in the Bible, but Jonah set his sights on Tarshish, far to the west by sea.
Jonah did not flee toward Jerusalem. He headed for the sea instead.
Damascus is not part of Jonah's flight. He boarded a ship bound for Tarshish.

questions.text: What happened at sea while Jonah was fleeing?

options.text: A thick fog hid the ship for days
options.explanation: The trouble was not fog. It was a violent storm sent by the Lord.

options.text: A great storm arose and threatened to break the ship
options.explanation: Jonah 1:4 says the Lord sent out a great wind, and there was a mighty tempest, so the ship was likely to be broken.

options.text: Pirates boarded and took the cargo
options.explanation: There are no pirates in Jonah. The danger came from a God-sent storm.

options.text: The ship ran aground on rocks
options.explanation: The ship did not run aground. It was caught in a fierce storm at sea.

questions.text: What did the sailors do to try to calm the storm?

options.text: They sacrificed a goat on the deck
options.explanation: They did offer a sacrifice to the Lord later, but only after the storm had stopped, not to calm it.

options.text: They threw Jonah into the sea
options.explanation: After casting lots that fell on Jonah, and at his own word, the sailors took him up and cast him into the sea, and the raging stopped (Jonah 1:15).

options.text: They turned the ship back to shore
options.explanation: They rowed hard to reach land but could not, so they finally cast Jonah overboard.

options.text: They lowered all the sails and waited
options.explanation: They lightened the ship by throwing cargo overboard, but the calm came when Jonah went into the sea.

questions.text: What did God prepare to swallow Jonah?

options.explanation: Jonah 1:17 says, "the LORD had prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah." He was inside it three days and three nights.
The text says a great fish, not a whale, and it is not named. Leviathan appears in other passages.
Jonah was swallowed by a great fish that God prepared, not a serpent.
The Bible simply calls it a great fish. A squid is not mentioned.

questions.text: How long was Jonah inside the great fish?

options.explanation: Jonah 1:17 gives the span as three days and three nights. Jesus later pointed to this as a sign.
The number was three days and three nights, not seven.
It was longer than a day. The text says three days and three nights.
Forty days was the warning Jonah later preached to Nineveh, not the time in the fish.

questions.text: What did Jonah do inside the fish?

options.explanation: Jonah slept earlier, down in the ship during the storm. Inside the fish he prayed.
Jonah 2 is his prayer from inside the fish. He cried out in his distress, and the Lord heard him.
Inside the fish, Jonah turned to prayer, not blame.

options.text: He wrote a letter to Nineveh
options.explanation: There is no letter. Jonah prayed, and then was delivered to preach in person.

questions.text: After being delivered, how many days did Jonah say Nineveh had before judgment?

options.explanation: Three days and three nights was his time in the fish, not the warning to Nineveh.
The number Jonah preached was forty, not ten.
Jonah 3:4 records his message: "Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown."
Jonah gave a forty-day warning, not a hundred.

questions.text: How did the people of Nineveh respond to Jonah's preaching?

options.text: They mocked him and drove him out
options.explanation: Far from mocking him, the people of Nineveh took the warning seriously.
They did not ignore it. The whole city repented.

options.text: They believed God and repented in sackcloth
options.explanation: Jonah 3 says the people believed God, proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from the greatest to the least. Even the king stepped down from his throne.
They did not crown Jonah. They humbled themselves before God, and He spared the city.

questions.text: How did Jonah feel when God spared Nineveh?

options.explanation: Jonah 4:1 says it displeased Jonah exceedingly, and he was very angry. He even said he would rather die than see his enemies spared.

options.text: He threw a feast to celebrate
options.explanation: Jonah did not celebrate. He was deeply upset that God showed mercy.
Jonah did not leave content. He sat outside the city, angry and waiting to see what would happen.

options.text: He asked to preach in more cities
options.explanation: Jonah did not ask for more work. He was grieved that Nineveh was spared.

questions.text: What plant did God provide to give Jonah shade, only to let it wither the next day?

options.explanation: The plant was a gourd, not a fig tree.
Jonah 4:6 says the Lord prepared a gourd to shade Jonah's head. The next day a worm struck it, and it withered, teaching Jonah about God's compassion.
It was a gourd that grew up over Jonah, not a grapevine.
A cedar is a tall tree, but the plant in Jonah's story was a fast-growing gourd.

scoring.perfectMessage: You know Jonah's whole journey, start to finish!

gradeBands.label: Setting Sail
gradeBands.message: Jonah is a short read with a big lesson. Give it a try.

gradeBands.label: Seasoned
gradeBands.message: You really know the runaway prophet.
